correctness.rationale: The change \(q=-\log(1-x),\ p=-y\) is invertible for \(x<1\) and preserves physical time, giving \(\dot q=p\), \(\dot p=e^{-q}-1\), and conserved \(H=p^2/2+q+e^{-q}-1\). The coercive strictly convex potential yields a unique closed energy oval. Positive turning point satisfies \(a_E=E+1+o(1)\); negative turning magnitude \(r_E=O(\log E)\). Exact identity \(E-V(a_E-w)=w-e^{-a_E}(e^w-1)\) bounds positive descent uniformly between \(\sqrt{2w}\) and \(\sqrt{2w}/\sqrt{1-\eta_E}\), \(\eta_E=O(E^{-1})\). On the negative branch \(E-V(-r_E+w)=(E+r_E+1)(1-e^{-w})-w\), yielding \(t_-=O(\log E/\sqrt E)\), while \(t_+=\sqrt{2E}(1+O(E^{-1}))\). Thus negative excursion shrinks in normalized phase; positive branch gives the uniform parabolic limit. The energy identity and sign of \(p\) yield the asserted pointwise-off-midpoint and dominated \(L^1\) momentum limit. Since \(x(sT)ds=-(\sqrt{2E}/T)dP_E\), integration by parts transfers the momentum jump to signed measure \(ds-\delta_{1/2}\). For all continuous tests the extension is justified by \(x\le1\), zero mean over an orbit, hence \(\int|x|ds\le2\). Pushforward density is the two-branch inverse derivative of the limiting parabola. The inspected \(check.py\) makes only bounded finite quadrature sanity checks and is not relied on as asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The signed mass-one force impulse in unmodified physical time describes a singular boundary layer of a classic integrable Loud/Toda oscillator and determines an exact phase-statistical law. This supplies qualitative limiting information not obtained from the known period asymptotic, with a motivated dynamical observable and nontrivial weak-* normalization.

final_claim: For the Loud system \(\dot x=-y(1-x),\ \dot y=x\) on \(x<1\) at energy \(E>0\), choose phase zero at the positive turning point, physical minimal period \(T(E)\), and define \(Q_E(s)=-\log(1-x(sT(E)))/E\), \(P_E(s)=-y(sT(E))/\sqrt{2E}\). As \(E\to\infty\), \(T(E)/(2\sqrt{2E})\to1\), \(Q_E\) converges uniformly to \(1-4s^2\) before midpoint and \(1-4(1-s)^2\) afterward, \(P_E\) converges in \(L^1\) to \(-2s\) before midpoint and \(2(1-s)\) afterward, the signed physical-time observable satisfies \(x(sT(E))\,ds\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}ds-\delta_{1/2}\), and the time-sampling pushforward of \(Q_E\) converges to the density \(1/(2\sqrt{1-u})\) on \((0,1)\).
limitations: Single reversible Loud parameter and invariant half-plane \(x<1\), not the complete quadratic-center family.
Convergence of physical-coordinate observables is weak-* as signed measures, not density \(L^1\); no finite-energy uniform rates claimed.
